passage.quote:
A schedule chooses one thread to take the next step; no
simultaneous or lockstep hardware execution is assumed.

summary: Execute actual fetched instructions from several groups against one global array, with private scratch and barriers and checked per-group thread limits.
Prove pointwise copy, multiplication and sensitivity gating correct for every completed admitted grid execution; separately construct admitted executions, including explicit padding storage.

Derive row-distributed dense forward outputs and TorchLean error bounds from actual combined admission and completion; construct finite admitted executions separately, then compose bounded-group backward stages without a hardware progress claim.

from.quote:
A grid step selects one group and one of its threads, fetches its instruction,
and uses the existing mixed integer and floating-point instruction semantics.
The selected group sees the actual current global array. Its resulting global
array becomes the grid's global array, while its local state is written back.
Other groups retain their registers, scratch memory and barrier state. Their
next instruction sees the updated global array. This is instruction-level
interleaving, not atomic execution of a whole group.

passage.quote:
inductive Step (cfg : Config n) (program : List Instr) : State groups n → List (Event groups n) → State groups n → Prop
  | issue (g : Fin groups) (thread : Fin n) (candidate : Option Word) (out : Outcome n)
      (step : Parallel.Step (cfg.group g) program candidate thread (view s g) out) :
      Step cfg program s (tag g out.events) (install s g out.state)
inductive Runs (cfg : Config n) (program : List Instr) : State groups n → List (Event groups n) → State groups n → Prop
  | nil : Runs cfg program s [] s
  | cons : Step cfg program s events middle → Runs cfg program middle rest final → Runs cfg program s (events++rest) final

from.quote:
For programs using only global memory and no barriers, the proof can give every
(group, thread) pair a unique flat thread number. Flattening preserves every
fetched instruction and actual global-memory update; it introduces no hardware
thread group and no new synchronization. This permits reuse of the existing
memory graph and independent-thread arithmetic proofs. Shared-memory or barrier
programs cannot use this simplification: they retain private storage identities
and group-specific arrival histories.

    (run : Runs cfg program s events final) (only : ∀ i ∈ program, GlobalOnly i) (idle : IdleBarriers s) :
    Parallel.Runs flatCfg program (flatten s) (flatEvents events) (flatten final) :=

from.quote:
For pointwise copy, multiplication and ReLU sensitivity gating, every completed
admitted grid execution stores the specified result, preserves the source words
and the allocation length, and uses aligned addresses within allocated storage.
A separate theorem constructs such an execution for every input word sequence
that meets the storage bounds. The total thread count can exceed 1,024; each
group has at most 1,024 threads. For a partially used final group, spare lanes
read an explicitly allocated source word and write distinct padding outputs.
Those outputs require allocated storage and are excluded from the logical
vector; they are not promised to retain their initial contents. Zero groups
have an explicit no-launch case.

passage.quote:
theorem launch_correct (run : Launch op l before after) :
    (∀ t, ∃ value, after[l.output t]?=some value ∧ Pointwise.Result op before[l.left t]! before[l.right t]! value) ∧
    (∀ i, i<l.prefixWords → after[i]?=before[i]?) ∧ after.length=before.length :=

from.quote:
The row-distributed dense program has a complete launch contract. Every completed
admitted combined execution stores the prescribed reduction results, preserves
its operands, and performs aligned accesses within allocated arrays. Its proof
derives input reads, scratch producers, barrier ordering and unique output
writers from that same trace. A separate finite construction reaches every
thread's exit and supplies read sources and write ordering satisfying the
combined memory constraints. It also covers an empty grid.

passage.quote:
theorem completed_forward (s : Dense.Shape) (b : Bounds s) (global : List Word)
    (seeds : Fin s.threads → Scalar.State) {events : List (Grid.Event s.rows s.width)} {final : Grid.State s.rows s.width}
    (run : Grid.Runs (config s b) (program s) (initial s global seeds) events final)
    (halted : ∀ g t, ((final.blocks g).lanes t).halted=true) (source co)
    (valid : Admitted s global seeds events source co) :
    (∀ row : Fin s.rows, ∃ value, final.global[s.outputBase+row.val]?=some value ∧ Output s global row.val value) ∧
    (∀ i, i<s.outputBase → final.global[i]?=global[i]?) ∧
    final.global.length=global.length ∧ (∀ g, (final.blocks g).shared.length=s.sharedWords) ∧
    (∀ event ∈ events, Grid.AccessSafe (initial s global seeds) event) :=

    (source co) (valid : Admitted s global seeds events source co)
    (g : Fin s.rows) (phase : Phase events g) (p q : Nat) (writer reader : Fin s.width)
    (storeOcc loadOcc : Scalar.Occurrence) (stored loaded : MemoryEffect)
    (atP : events[p]?=some (g,.scalar writer (some .shared) storeOcc))

theorem universal_forward (s : Dense.Shape) (bounds : GridDense.Bounds s) (global : List Word)
    (seeds : Fin s.threads → Ptx.Scalar.State)
    (x : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.column s.columns))
    (w : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.matrix s.rows s.columns))
    (b : Tensor ℝ (DenseVJP.column s.rows)) (encoding : Encoding s global x w b)
    {events : List (Grid.Event s.rows s.width)} {final : Grid.State s.rows s.width}
    (run : Grid.Runs (GridDense.config s bounds) (Dense.program s) (GridDense.initial s global seeds) events final)
    (halted : ∀ g t, ((final.blocks g).lanes t).halted=true) (source co)
    (valid : GridDense.Admitted s global seeds events source co) :
    (∀ row : Fin s.rows, ∃ value, final.global[s.outputBase+row.val]?=some value ∧
      finiteReal value=some (max (encoding.row row).affine 0) ∧
      |max (encoding.row row).affine 0-
        Spec.get2 ((DenseVJP.graph s.rows s.columns).forward (DenseVJP.inputs x w b)) row 0| ≤ (encoding.row row).error) ∧
    (∀ i, i<s.outputBase → final.global[i]?=global[i]?) ∧
    final.global.length=global.length ∧ (∀ g, (final.blocks g).shared.length=s.sharedWords) ∧
    (∀ event ∈ events, Grid.AccessSafe (GridDense.initial s global seeds) event) :=

from.quote:
For finite execution witnesses, a selected schedule may read the current arrays.
A checked replay must then recover every read's last preceding store, or its
initial cell, across the combined trace. Giving those stores chronological
order supplies a sufficient memory-admission certificate, including actual
within-group barrier edges. This construction does not change the permitted
candidate reads or assert that every admitted execution follows that schedule.
The dense witness runs one group at a time. Within that group it executes each
lane's product segment, completes the barrier, repeats the reduction segments
and their barriers, and then executes the output segments and exits. Physical
lane numbers select registers and barrier participants; logical row-and-column
indices determine arithmetic and addresses. The construction must prove both
parts agree, without applying the 1,024-thread group limit to the grid total.
Address-representation and allocation bounds still apply.

passage.quote:
inductive ConcreteRuns (cfg : Config n) (program : List Instr) : State groups n → List (Event groups n) → State groups n → Prop
  | nil : ConcreteRuns cfg program s [] s
  | cons (g : Fin groups) (thread : Fin n) (out : Outcome n)
      (step : Parallel.Step (cfg.group g) program none thread (view s g) out)
      (rest : ConcreteRuns cfg program (install s g out.state) events final) :
      ConcreteRuns cfg program s (tag g out.events++events) final
